title: THIS_AND_FUTURE Truncation and Splitting on Series Containing RDATEs

citations.verbatim_quote: The recurrence set is generated by considering the initial "DTSTART" property along with the "RRULE", "RDATE", and "EXDATE" properties contained within the recurring component.  The "DTSTART" property defines the first instance in the recurrence set.  The "DTSTART" property value SHOULD match the pattern of the recurrence rule, if specified.  The recurrence set generated with a "DTSTART" property value that doesn't match the pattern of the rule is undefined.  The final recurrence set is generated by gathering all of the start DATE-TIME values generated by any of the specified "RRULE" and "RDATE" properties, and then excluding any start DATE-TIME values specified by "EXDATE" properties.

The UNTIL rule part defines a DATE or DATE-TIME value that bounds the recurrence rule in an inclusive manner.  If the value specified by UNTIL is synchronized with the specified recurrence, this DATE or DATE-TIME becomes the last instance of the recurrence.

The parameter specifies the effective range of recurrence instances that is specified by the property.  The effective range is from the recurrence identifier specified by the property.  If this parameter is not specified on an allowed property, then the default range is the single instance specified by the recurrence identifier value of the property.  The parameter value can only be "THISANDFUTURE" to indicate a range defined by the recurrence identifier and all subsequent instances.

rationale: Under RFC 5545 Section 3.8.5.2, the recurrence set of a component is the union of occurrences generated by `RRULE` and occurrences explicitly listed in `RDATE` (minus `EXDATE`). Meanwhile, under RFC 5545 Section 3.3.10, the `UNTIL` rule part inside an `RRULE` bounds only the `RRULE` evaluation—it does NOT filter or suppress `RDATE` values on the same component. Consequently, when a calendar store implements `THIS_AND_FUTURE` deletion or splitting (per RFC 5545 Section 3.2.13, affecting the target recurrence identifier and all subsequent instances), merely setting `RRULE.UNTIL = split_dtstart - 1s` on the prior component is insufficient if that component also contains `RDATE` entries at or after `split_dtstart` (or if the series is defined purely by `RDATE`s with `rrule=None`). To prevent deleted or split-off future `RDATE` occurrences from still being emitted by the prior component, the store must also prune `RDATE` values `>= split_dtstart` from the truncated prior component (and, on a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` edit, partition `RDATE` values `>= split_dtstart` onto the forked future component if not superseded).
store_implication: When `delete` or `edit` is invoked with `recurrence_id=split_rid` and `THIS_AND_FUTURE` range on a recurring component that contains `RDATE` values: (1) On `delete(THIS_AND_FUTURE)`: in addition to bounding `rrule.until` to `split_dtstart - delta` (when `rrule` is present), the store MUST remove from the prior component's `rdate` list all `RDATE` entries whose start timestamp (normalized to the component's timezone or DATE type) is `>= split_dtstart`; if the component has no `rrule` and `split_dtstart == dtstart`, the entire component is deleted. (2) On `edit(THIS_AND_FUTURE)`: the prior component's `rdate` list MUST retain only `RDATE` entries strictly `< split_dtstart`, and the newly forked future component MUST NOT retain prior `RDATE` entries `< split_dtstart` (retaining only `RDATE` entries `>= split_dtstart`, or the explicit `rdate` list provided in the edit patch).
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Recurring component with `RRULE:FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=3` (May 1..3) AND `RDATE:20250510T090000`: deleting `20250502T090000` with `THIS_AND_FUTURE` range MUST both truncate `RRULE` to `UNTIL=20250502T085959` AND remove `2025-05-10T09:00:00` from `RDATE`. If `RDATE` is left untouched on the master component, `2025-05-10T09:00:00` erroneously survives a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` deletion from May 2.

Deleting `THIS_AND_FUTURE` specifically targeting an `RDATE` occurrence (e.g. `split_rid = 20250510T090000` when `RRULE` ended on May 3): `RRULE` occurrences `< May 10` remain intact while all `RDATE` values `>= 2025-05-10T09:00:00` are removed from `RDATE`.

Splitting a series via `edit(THIS_AND_FUTURE)` at May 2 when the master had `RDATE`s at `2025-04-28T09:00:00` (before split) and `2025-05-10T09:00:00` (after split): the prior component retains only `2025-04-28T09:00:00` and the forked future component retains only `2025-05-10T09:00:00` (so neither RDATE is duplicated across both segments or leaked into the wrong segment).

scenarios.name: delete_this_and_future_prunes_rdate_occurrences_at_or_after_split
scenarios.description: Deleting from May 2 with THIS_AND_FUTURE range on a daily series (May 1..3) that also has a future RDATE on May 10 truncates the RRULE UNTIL bound before May 2 AND removes the May 10 RDATE so only May 1 remains on the timeline.
